text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 diagnostics involve tests that detect current infection with the SARS-CoV-2 virus. These tests can be broadly categorized into viral tests (molecular and antigen tests) and antibody tests. Viral tests, like PCR and antigen tests, identify active infections, while antibody tests detect past infections by identifying antibodies produced by the body in response to the virus.

list.title: Molecular tests (NAATs, including RT-PCR):
list.snippet: These are highly accurate and detect the virus's genetic material. They are usually performed in a laboratory.

list.title: Antigen tests:
list.snippet: These tests detect viral proteins and are often used as rapid tests, providing results quickly.
